## What Is AI Usage Monitoring?


AI usage monitoring is the practice of tracking how generative AI is actually used across your organization: which tools, by how many people, how frequently, and when they first and last appeared. It answers the question every security and compliance team now gets from leadership — “what AI are we actually using?” — with evidence instead of a survey. It’s the foundation for an AI acceptable-use policy, vendor review, and any decision about what to allow or block.


## What You Should Actually Monitor


Signal Why it matters


Which tools Discover the full set in use — not just ChatGPT, but Claude, Gemini, Perplexity, Copilot, Grok, and new ones


How many users Distinguish one curious employee from org-wide adoption


How often Visit frequency shows whether a tool is a habit or a one-off


First / last seen Catch newly-adopted tools and ones that have gone quiet


Sensitive-data exposure The real risk — what data is going into those tools (a DLP question)

## Privacy by Design: Usage, Not Content


Good AI usage monitoring shouldn’t mean surveilling employees. Strac records the platform **hostname and visit only** — not prompt text, replies, or files. A visit means a cataloged AI site was reached, not that anyone typed a prompt; a page left open in a background tab counts the same as active use. That keeps the view honest and privacy-respecting: you learn *which tools are in play* without reading anyone’s conversations.

## Beyond Which Tools: Monitor the Data

## 🌶️ Spicy FAQs on AI Usage Monitoring


### What is AI usage monitoring?


It's tracking how generative AI is used across your organization - which tools, how many users, how often, and when first/last seen. It gives security and compliance teams evidence of real AI adoption instead of a survey, and it's the foundation for any allow/block decision.


### How does Strac monitor AI usage?


Through its browser extension. It reports each cataloged AI platform a user reaches, and the Shadow AI dashboard aggregates it into a live view of tools by users and visits - working across networks and off-VPN, with no proxy and no network changes.


### Does AI usage monitoring read employees' prompts?


Not in Strac. It records the platform hostname and visit only - never prompt text, replies, or files. You learn which tools are in use without surveilling anyone's conversations.


### How is this different from shadow AI monitoring?


They overlap - shadow AI is the unsanctioned-tool angle, AI usage monitoring is the broader visibility view. Both come from the same browser telemetry; the difference is framing and what you do with it (govern all AI vs. surface the unapproved).


### Can I act on what I monitor?


Yes. From the dashboard you approve tools you sanction, block ones you don't, and leave the rest observed. Each action writes the settings the extension enforces on users' next sync - and you can layer DLP to protect data in the tools you allow.
